newsitem.title: USA: InVision expects to make profit in 1997.
newsitem.headline: InVision expects to make profit in 1997.

text.p: InVision Technologies Inc, which went public in April, Friday said it expects to break into profitability in 1997 after winning a $52 million Federal Aviation Administration contract for 54 explosive detection systems.

"Certainly, the company is close to the breakeven stage and this (contract) will push the company into profitability in 1997," said David Pillor, a senior vice president at InVision. "The world market follows closely FAA decisions and we anticipate significant gains on the international marketplace that will continue to propel our growth.
Pillor said InVision will report a 1996 loss.

In the award announced late Thursday, the FAA contract calls for the company to deliver the first unit in January and the rest over 12 months. The government has the option to buy more systems in the second year which would boost the contract's value to $110.9 million.

Pillor said there has been no decision yet on which U.S. airports will get the CTX-5000 SP equipment -- the first and only explosive detection system for inspecting checked baggage that has passed FAA certification.
"It's safe to say the systems will be spread around category 'X' airports -- those considered the highest risk airports by the U.S. government. There are 19 category 'X' airports," he said.

Pillor said the company's CTX device is currently installed in San Francisco, Atlanta and New York airports. Outside the United States, the devices can be found in airports in Tel Aviv, the United Kingdom, Brussels and Japan. Machines are now being installed in airports in France, he added.
He said the machines currently can screen 300 bags per hour and expects that to increase to 400 bags per hour by the end of 1997.
